drug_class: Antibiotic and Corticosteroid Combination (Eye Drop or Ointment)
purpose: This medication is used to treat eye infections that also cause redness, swelling, or irritation. It combines an antibiotic to fight bacteria with a steroid to reduce inflammation. Your doctor may prescribe it after eye surgery or for certain bacterial eye infections.
how_it_works: Tobramycin is an antibiotic that kills the bacteria causing your eye infection by stopping the bacteria from making the proteins they need to survive. Dexamethasone is a steroid that calms down the swelling, redness, and discomfort in your eye. Together, they fight the infection and help your eye feel better faster.
common_side_effects: Some people may notice temporary stinging or burning right after putting the drops in. You might also experience blurred vision for a short time, eye irritation, itching, or a mild increase in eye pressure with long-term use. These effects are usually mild and temporary.
warnings: Do not wear contact lenses while using this medication unless your doctor says it is okay. Do not use this in your eyes if you have a viral eye infection like pink eye caused by a virus, or a fungal eye infection, as the steroid part can make those worse. Using steroid eye drops for too long can raise the pressure in your eye, which may harm your vision — so always follow your doctor's instructions and attend follow-up appointments. Tell your doctor if your symptoms do not improve after a few days.
typical_dosing: The usual dose for the eye drops is 1 to 2 drops in the affected eye every 4 to 6 hours. During the first day or two, your doctor may have you use it more often, such as every 2 hours while awake. For the ointment, a small amount is usually applied to the eye 3 to 4 times a day. Always follow the exact instructions your doctor gives you and finish the full course even if your eye feels better.
